translationRepairs: Earlier, after Wang Hua died and Xu Tanshou passed away as well, General of the Palace Guard Yin Jingren, seeing that talented men were dying off, reported to Taizu recommending that Zhan be summoned to court.

Earlier, after Wang Hua died and Wang Tanshou passed away as well, General of the Palace Guard Yin Jingren, seeing that talented men were dying off, reported to Taizu recommending that Zhan be summoned to court.
The Chinese has 曇首, referring to Wang Tanshou from s0031, not Xu Tanshou.

At that time the Emperor was in the Yancian Hall and sent a messenger to question Ye: "Because you have some literary talent, you were entrusted and promoted; the titles and ranks you hoped for were not few by precedent.

At that time the Emperor was in the Yanxian Hall and sent a messenger to question Ye: "Because you have some literary talent, you were entrusted and promoted; the titles and ranks you hoped for were not few by precedent.
延賢堂 is Yanxian Hall; "Yancian" is a romanization/typing error in the hall name.

Ye's wife came down first and comforted her child, then turned and cursed Ye: "You spare no thought for your aged mother-in-law, you show no gratitude for the emperor's grace and favor—your death alone could never atone for this crime, so why must you wrongfully destroy our children and descendants?"

Ye's wife came down first and comforted her child, then turned and cursed Ye: "You spare no thought for your hundred-year-old mother, you show no gratitude for the emperor's grace and favor—your death alone could never atone for this crime, so why must you wrongfully destroy our children and descendants?"
阿家 is Ye's mother from Ye's perspective in this rebuke, not Ye's mother-in-law; the current English reverses the relationship.

Ye's wife came down first and stroked her child; turning back she cursed Ye, saying: "You do not think of your aged mother-in-law who may live a hundred years, you feel no gratitude for the Son of Heaven's grace and favor—death by itself surely cannot atone for the crime; why must you wrongfully kill our children and descendants?"

Ye's wife came down first and stroked her child; turning back she cursed Ye, saying: "You do not think of your hundred-year-old mother, you feel no gratitude for the Son of Heaven's grace and favor—death by itself surely cannot atone for the crime; why must you wrongfully kill our children and descendants?"
阿家 in this sentence is the mother whose old age Ye failed to consider; "mother-in-law" gives the wrong relationship to Ye.
His wife said: "I am the guilty one—mother-in-law, do not grieve over this."
His wife said: "He is a condemned man. Mother, do not waste another thought on him."
罪人 refers to Ye, not to the wife herself; the current idiomatic English makes the wife call herself guilty.
His crimes exceed those of Zhou and Yan a hundredfold, his excesses surpass those of Wang Mang tenfold—since the beginning of history, nothing like this has been heard.
His crimes exceed those of Han Zhuo and Yi a hundredfold, his excesses surpass those of Huan Xuan and Wang Mang tenfold—since the beginning of history, nothing like this has been heard.
Chinese 過十玄、莽 names both Huan Xuan (玄) and Wang Mang (莽); the English omits 玄 and only has Wang Mang. Also 浞、豷 are Han Zhuo and Yi, not Zhou and Yan.
His crimes exceed a hundredfold those of Zhou and Yan, his excesses surpass tenfold those of Xuan and Mang—since the opening of the age, none such as this has been heard.
His crimes are a hundredfold those of Han Zhuo and Yi; his excesses are tenfold those of Huan Xuan and Wang Mang—since the opening of the age, none such as this has been heard.
Literal English leaves 玄、莽 as bare Xuan and Mang; expand to Huan Xuan and Wang Mang, and render 浞、豷 as Han Zhuo and Yi.
His wife said: "A guilty man—mother-in-law, do not dwell on it."
His wife said: "A condemned man. Mother, do not think of him."
罪人 refers to the condemned Fan Ye, while 阿家 directly addresses his mother; the former literal wording obscured both references.
